reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 10586, signed January 13, 1955, states that Executive Order No. 8714 of March 18, 1941 "is hereby revoked". The wording has no effective-date clause, so the recorded date is the signing date 1955-01-13 (the order was filed with the Federal Register on January 13, 1955 and printed January 15, 1955, the alternative reading). The revocation reaches the three succession designations and the clause revoking EO 6202-B, which had been performed at issue.

Terminated by express revocation. EO 9830, Part III, revokes the listed Executive orders including "No. 8937 of November 7, 1941." The enacting clause orders EO 9830 "it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:" so the end is recorded as 1947-05-01. Part III has no separate date and the enacting clause orders Parts I, II and III alike 'effective May 1, 1947'; the alternative reading is that the revocation took effect on signing, 1947-02-24 (printed 12 FR 1259, 1947-02-25). Later event (amendment, clause continues as amended): EO 9579 restated the proviso, effective as of December 8, 1944 ("This order shall be effective as of December 8, 1944."). Before: "Provided, that such persons shall notify the Civil Service Commission within forty days after their service in the armed forces has terminated that they desire to have the benefits of this order." After: "Provided, That such persons shall notify the Civil Service Commission within 90 days after termination of their service in the armed forces or of hospitalization continuing after discharge for a period of not more than one year." The change lengthens the notice period and adds hospitalization; the substance of the proviso changed.
